item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00193","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C24","C01","C05"],"selected_candidate_label":"C24","confidence":0.97,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C24 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Its first section uses the distinctive structure of naming a department head and, as designated by that official, subordinate officers, then declaring them “designated and empowered to perform” presidential functions. The child closely adapts that machinery for the Attorney General and Assistant Attorneys General. C24 also contains an almost verbatim definitions provision using the same ordered list and the same perform/exercise construction. C01 and C05 share the delegation and definitions formula, but not C24’s especially probative combination of subordinate-designation structure and near-identical definitional language.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The Attorney General, and, as designated by the Attorney General for this purpose, any Assistant Attorney General are hereby designated and empowered to perform the functions conferred ... upon the President","parent_excerpt":"The Secretary of Defense, and, as designated by the said Secretary for this purpose, any of the Secretaries, Under Secretaries, and Assistant Secretaries of the military departments, are hereby designated and empowered to perform the following-described functions of the President","explanation":"The child reproduces the parent’s distinctive sequence: principal officer, subordinate officers designated by that principal for the purpose, and authorization to perform presidential functions."},{"child_excerpt":"the term \"functions\" includes duties, powers, responsibilities, authority, and discretion, and the term \"perform\" may be construed to include \"exercise\"","parent_excerpt":"the term \"functions\" includes duties, powers, responsibilities, authority, and discretion, and the term \"perform\" may be construed to mean \"exercise\"","explanation":"This is nearly verbatim language with the same five-item definition in the same order; only “include” replaces “mean” in the final clause."}]}
